messages.subject: inlabru: replicating effects
parts:
Dear INLA users,

I am trying to use inlabru for multiple likelihoods. In particular, I am trying to understand how to conduct some features that R-INLA provides for copying and replicating effects. Here a reproducible example for the copy one (using the scale parameter feature) assuming different intercepts:

# Simulate data: 2 groups with same AR1 param

n = 500

rho <- 0.8

intercept <- c(1, -1)

x1 = arima.sim(n=n, model=list(ar=c(rho)))

x2 = arima.sim(n=n, model=list(ar=c(rho)))

sd <- c(0.01, 0.01)

# Gaussian observations

set.seed(10)

y1 = rnorm(n, mean = intercept[1] + x1, sd = sd[1])

y2 = rnorm(n, mean = intercept[2] + x2, sd = sd[2])

mydata <- data.frame(y1, y2, t = 1:n)

 

#Effects

cmp1 <- ~ Intercept1 +     Intercept2 +

    + arima1(t, model = "ar1") +

    + arima2(t, copy = "arima1", fixed = FALSE)

 #Formula for each linear predictor

formula1 <- y1 ~ Intercept1 + arima1

formula2 <- y2 ~ Intercept2 + arima2

 # Likelihoods

like1 <- like(formula1,

    data = mydata,

    family = "gaussian")

 like2 <- like(formula2,

    data = mydata,

    family = "gaussian")

 # Fitting

fit <- bru(cmp1,

           like1,

           like2)

summary(fit)

I have tried to conduct same for replicate but without success. I’ve tried with a similar structure than before, but now, changing cmp1, formula1 and formula2.

#Effects

r <- rep(1:2, each = n)

cmp1 <- ~ Intercept1 +

  Intercept2  + myar1(map = t, model = "ar1", replicate = r, n = n, values = 1:n)

# Formula

formula1 <- y1 ~ Intercept1 + myar1(map = t, model = "ar1",

                                    replicate = r, n = n, values = 1:n)

formula2 <- y2 ~ Intercept2 + myar1(map = t, model = "ar1",

                                    replicate = r, n = n, values = 1:n)

It would be nice if you could help me in solving the issue.

Thanks,

Joaquín.

In the latest version, the code gave me these messages:

"
Warning in add_mapper(component$main, label = component$label, lhoods = lh, :
All covariate evaluations for 'Intercept1' are NULL; an intercept
component was likely intended.
Implicit latent intercept component specification is deprecated
since version 2.1.14.
Use explicit notation '+ Intercept1(1)' instead.
Warning in add_mapper(component$main, label = component$label, lhoods = lh, :
All covariate evaluations for 'Intercept2' are NULL; an intercept
component was likely intended.
Implicit latent intercept component specification is deprecated
since version 2.1.14.
Use explicit notation '+ Intercept2(1)' instead.
Warning in handle_problems(e_input) :
The input evaluation 'Intercept1' for 'Intercept1' failed. Perhaps
the data object doesn't contain the needed variables? Falling back to
'1'.
Warning in handle_problems(e_input) :
The input evaluation 'Intercept2' for 'Intercept2' failed. Perhaps
the data object doesn't contain the needed variables? Falling back to
'1'.
"

You're using old, deprecated behavior; as the warnings in this case
accurately say, you need to be specific about the component inputs.
I would suggest the following change:

cmp1 <- ~ 0 + Intercept1(1) + Intercept2(1) +

+ arima1(t, model = "ar1") +
+ arima2(t, copy = "arima1", fixed = FALSE)
Finn

Hi Finn,
Thank you so much for the quick answer. But, I was mainly referring to the replicate feature. I get the following error:
Error in row_kron(sub_A[[k + 1]], A_) : Size mismatch for row.kron, (n1, n2) = (1000, 500)

An the code employed has been:

# Simulate data: 2 groups with same AR1 param

n = 500

rho <- 0.8

intercept <- c(1, -1)

x1 = arima.sim(n=n, model=list(ar=c(rho)))

x2 = arima.sim(n=n, model=list(ar=c(rho)))

sd <- c(0.01, 0.01)

# Gaussian observations

set.seed(10)

y1 = rnorm(n, mean = intercept[1] + x1, sd = sd[1])

y2 = rnorm(n, mean = intercept[2] + x2, sd = sd[2])

mydata <- data.frame(y1, y2, t = 1:n)
# Model

r <- rep(1:2, each = n)
cmp1 <- ~ Intercept1 +
  Intercept2 +
    + myar1(map = t, model = "ar1", replicate = r, n = n, values = 1:n)

formula1 <- y1 ~ Intercept1 + myar1(map = t, model = "ar1",
                                    replicate = r, n = n, values = 1:n)
formula2 <- y2 ~ Intercept2 + myar1(map = t, model = "ar1",
                                    replicate = r, n = n, values = 1:n)

like1 <- like(formula1,
    data = mydata,
    family = "gaussian")

like2 <- like(formula2,
    data = mydata,
    family = "gaussian")

fit <- bru(cmp1,
           like1,
           like2)
summary(fit)

It seems that it is related with the dimension, and then, the way I am introducing the replication in the model... But, I don't know how to solve the issue in inlabru.
Thanks so much.
Joaquín.

parts:
Then second model, are you trying to use one replicate for y1, and
another for y2?
The natural approach is to supply the data that is needed for each
observation model:

mydata1 <- mydata2 <- mydata
mydata1$repl <- 1
mydata2$repl <- 2
cmp1 <- ~ 0 + Intercept1(1) + Intercept2(1) +
myar(t, model = "ar1", replicate = repl)

# Formula

formula1 <- y1 ~ Intercept1 + myar
formula2 <- y2 ~ Intercept2 + myar

like1 <- like(formula1,
data = mydata1,

family = "gaussian")

like2 <- like(formula2,
data = mydata2,

family = "gaussian")

fit <- bru(cmp1,
like1,
like2)
summary(fit)
